content.intro: In this lesson, you will study choosing a java code editor with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you make sure your terminal and editor use the JDK you intend to learn and build with. In this lesson, focus on basic text editors and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A setup is correct only when the selected runtime and compiler match the intended JDK. Check `java -version` and `javac -version` separately, and verify PATH/JAVA_HOME rather than guessing which installation is active. Apply that reasoning specifically to basic text editors and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.title: Visual Studio Code and Java extensions
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

items.title: IntelliJ IDEA
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Relate the JDK tools to the source-to-program workflow. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
